aswang.name: Aswang
aswang.summary: A shape-shifter that lives as an ordinary neighbor by day and hunts by night.
lore_clues: Families hang garlic and salt above the doorway after dusk. The kind widow next door never joins the evening gathering.
The old stories say an aswang looks like any neighbor until you are close. Dogs and roosters know first.
Garlic is the oldest defense. Show it, and the disguise breaks.
aswang.lure_text: A neighbor's voice calls your name from the dark. You live alone.
aswang.banish_text: The disguise tears like wet paper. The thing wearing it flees into the night.
aswang.enrage_text: It laughs, and the laugh is no longer human.

onryo.name: Onryo
onryo.summary: A vengeful spirit that cannot rest. It moves only when it is not being watched.
lore_clues: The wet footprints stop whenever someone turns around, like the children's game of freezing when the watcher looks.
Priests say a grudge this strong cannot be argued with. It must be sealed.
Shrines sell paper talismans, ofuda, written to seal restless spirits.
onryo.lure_text: Wet footsteps. Behind you. Then silence.
onryo.banish_text: The paper burns white. The spirit folds into the floorboards and is still.
onryo.enrage_text: Your hands shake. It is not sealed. It is angry.

llorona.name: La Llorona
llorona.summary: A weeping woman in white who searches the river for the children she lost.
lore_clues: Children are told to be home before the weeping starts. The sound seems nearer the more you run.
She is not hunting you. She is searching. Anything small and lost draws her attention.
A grieving mother will stop for what belongs to her child. Offer her something that was a child's.
llorona.lure_text: Ay, mis hijos... The weeping is coming from every direction.
llorona.banish_text: She takes the little shoe and holds it to her chest. The weeping fades down the river.
llorona.enrage_text: That was not what she was looking for. The weeping becomes a scream.

pontianak.name: Pontianak
pontianak.summary: A vengeful spirit of a woman who died in childbirth. The scent of frangipani warns of her.
lore_clues: Frangipani flowers smell strongest when she is near. A baby crying alone in the night is never what it seems.
She lunges fast, then retreats. Keep your distance and watch for her hair.
Elders say a nail driven into the back of her neck ends her fury.
pontianak.lure_text: A baby cries nearby. The scent of frangipani turns sickly sweet.
pontianak.banish_text: The nail sinks in. She shudders, and the hunger leaves her face.
pontianak.enrage_text: Wrong. She shrieks and the frangipani smell chokes the air.

rusalka.name: Rusalka
rusalka.summary: The restless spirit of a drowned girl who lures travelers to the water's edge.
lore_clues: Villagers avoid the river in Rusal'na week, when the spirits come ashore to dance and sing.
If a rusalka asks you a riddle you cannot answer, she tickles you to death.
Travelers tuck wormwood into their clothes. The bitter smell drives them away.
rusalka.lure_text: A sweet song drifts over the reeds. Your feet turn toward it.
rusalka.banish_text: She recoils from the bitter herb and slips back beneath the water.
rusalka.enrage_text: The song turns shrill. Wrong remedy.

nuckelavee.name: Nuckelavee
nuckelavee.summary: A skinless horseman-beast from the sea whose breath withers crops and livestock.
lore_clues: Crofters say it wanders the shore, but never crosses running fresh water.
Even brave men would go miles out of their way to avoid it. It hates the burn, the stream of sweet water.
Fresh water is the one thing it will not pass.
nuckelavee.lure_text: Hooves on wet stone. The air smells like rot and brine.
nuckelavee.banish_text: It rears back from the water and bolts for the sea.
nuckelavee.enrage_text: That did nothing. It charges, furious.

tokoloshe.name: Tokoloshe
tokoloshe.summary: A small mischievous spirit said to attack sleepers. You mostly see it when it wants to be seen.
lore_clues: Many families raise their beds off the floor. Somebody always insists on it.
It is small and cannot reach a high bed. It waits at the foot of the bed.
Bricks under the bed legs keep a sleeper out of its reach.
tokoloshe.lure_text: A giggle at floor level. Something small scrapes under the bed.
tokoloshe.banish_text: You stack the bricks. It cannot reach. With a hiss, it is gone.
tokoloshe.enrage_text: Wrong again. Its giggle becomes a snarl.

wendigo.name: Wendigo
wendigo.summary: A winter spirit of insatiable hunger. In living tradition it is a serious subject; see the cultural notes in the README.
lore_clues: Winter tales say it hunts the starving and the greedy. It is drawn to the cold.
It is tall, gaunt, and always hungry. It is cold itself, and it fears warmth.
Fire is the answer in the stories. Keep a flame lit and carry it.
wendigo.lure_text: Branches break overhead. Something very tall is walking in the trees.
wendigo.banish_text: The torch flares. It howls, gaunt and pale, and the cold retreats with it.
wendigo.enrage_text: It was not afraid of that. It comes faster.
